page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 62,125.29 and a PassMark CPU score of 55,792.37, both placing in the top 25%. The memory subsystem exhibits strong performance in PassMark memory tests and database operations, while large-block memory read and write bandwidths remain average at 168.6 GB/sec and 68.03 GB/sec respectively. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is highly efficient at 294.35 GB/sec, whereas single-threaded compression and decompression tasks align with average performance tiers.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a compute-heavy hardware profile, offering high CPU density but limited memory capacity per core. This configuration is cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local SSD storage. The instance demonstrates strong capabilities in small-model LLM inference, processing 2,455.35 tokens per second for a 135M model, though performance drops to average levels for larger 7B models. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded data processing, web serving, database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
